record.name: Thermocompression with non-conductive film
record.role: Trace a bump-based TC-NCF route and separate polymer behavior from electrical contact formation.
record.description: Thermocompression bonding applies controlled temperature, force and alignment to form interconnections. In a TC-NCF route, a non-conductive film occupies the space between the mating dies while metallic bumps and pads carry the electrical connection. The polymer must deform and cure without blocking intended contacts or trapping unacceptable voids. Thin-die handling, film behavior and bump geometry are therefore coupled. TC-NCF is one thermocompression implementation, not a synonym for every bump process or every adhesive. Samsung’s February 2024 HBM3E 12H announcement gives a concrete historical application; it does not make one vendor’s process window universal.
mechanism: Prepare bumped dies, compatible film and verified surface/handling conditions.
Place the film at its defined wafer or die stage; maintain the intended contact openings and contamination controls.
Align a die to the receiving die and apply the qualified thermal/force cycle for metallic contact and polymer flow/cure.
Repeat the specified stacking sequence while tracking placement error and cumulative warpage.
Inspect continuity, bond-line condition and voids; complete the product-specific reliability qualification.

record.engineeringExample: Synthetic serial flow: 12 placements × (0.3 s alignment + 0.7 s bonding) plus 3 s handling occupy 15 s. A different station layout could overlap work; this calculation predicts neither commercial throughput nor yield.
record.evidenceNotes: Historical vendor example: Samsung reported an advanced TC-NCF route for its 2024 HBM3E 12H development. Sampling, qualification and volume production are distinct statuses.
